question: In covering a distance of 198 km, Amit takes 4 hours more than Vinay. If Amit doubles his speed, then he would take 5 hours less than Vinay. Amit's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Amit** doubles his speed (ratio 1 : 2), the time ratio becomes 2 : 1.

Difference in time units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

Actual time difference = 4 hours (more) + 5 hours (less) = 9 hours.

∴ 1 unit = 9 hours. Original time taken by **Amit** = 2 units = 18 hours.

**Amit**'s speed = Distance ÷ Original Time = 198 ÷ 18 = 11 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72e9676642ac068b9be37f43e969ab78b139593eb6cf78cfc455e8b047dcf97e.png] 

**Given:** Total distance = 198 km. Let **Amit**'s speed be 's' and **Vinay**'s time be 'T'.

⇒ Case 1: 198/s = T + 4

⇒ Case 2: 198/(2s) = T − 5

⇒ Subtracting Case 2 from Case 1: (198/s) − (198/2s) = (T + 4) − (T − 5)

⇒ 198/2s = 9

⇒ 198 = 18s

⇒ s = 198 ÷ 18

⇒ s = 11 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 11 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁). This is the core logic for ratio-based shortcuts.

Relative Speed

In same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed Formula

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).</p
